Thanks — we can definitely support this. Proposed approach to keep timelines aggressive while protecting sensitive details:

1) Mutual NDA first: I just routed a Redwood mutual NDA (Redwood_NDA_v3) through DocuSign; link below. We'll request basic assurance (standard mutual NDA, purpose-limited to review of security artifacts).

3) Full report: we will produce a redacted report for distribution removing: customer identifiers, exact hostnames/IPs (replaced with network ranges), removed PoC steps and scripts, and hashed service identifiers. We will also provide a redaction matrix explaining each removal.

4) Unredacted access: for auditor/Legal-only needs we can provide time-limited, read-only access to the full report in a secure session (no downloads), or an on-site review under a signed DPA/PA.

5) Remediation table: we will include a short status matrix (finding id, severity, remediation status, owner, ETA).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: security assessment artifacts for SIG/SOC2 evidence

Diego / Karthik —

I reviewed Jenna's request and Diego's proposed approach. My suggested redaction policy for external distribution:

- Remove: full IPv4/IPv6 addresses, fully-qualified hostnames, internal DNS entries, employee names or emails, customer-specific data (any unique identifiers that would reveal a customer).
- Replace: exact IPs/hostnames with anonymized ranges or tokenized labels (e.g., APP-SERVER-01 -> <app-server-01>).
- Remove PoC: any code snippets and step-by-step exploit artifacts. Retain a plain-language description of the vulnerability and impact classification.
- Maintain: CVE references (where public), severity classification, remediation status and high-level timeline.

Also: provide a separate redaction matrix (spreadsheet) that lists each redacted element and rationale; keep that matrix internal-only but provide a redacted summary of it to the customer.

If the customer requests academic-level granularity (for an auditor), we require a signed NDA + Data Processing Addendum and access via our secure viewer (no downloads). For particularly sensitive items we can do an in-person review with Legal present.

One other legal note: avoid creating an attachment that contains both redacted and unredacted content in the same file. Create explicit files: Exec_Summary_Redacted.pdf, Full_Report_Redacted.pdf, Full_Report_Unredacted.pdf (internal-only).

I'll prepare a short blurb we can send externally confirming redaction categories and access rules.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
